# World currencies — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/world-currencies.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/world-currencies.ttl`](../decks/world-currencies.ttl) · **Cards:** 193 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The currency of each of the 193 UN member states, with its ISO 4217 code: 193 cards with a country on the front and its currency on the back, in English and Swedish, such as Sweden → Swedish krona (SEK). Compiled from Wikidata and checked against the ISO 4217 lists of the maintenance agency SIX and the EU Interinstitutional Style Guide.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of states, the currency of each, the ISO codes and the English and Swedish names come from it, and where its labels were missing, outdated or malformed the wording is the author's own (currency names are facts; Zimbabwe Gold is the currency's official name). SIX's ISO 4217 lists (all rights reserved), the EU Interinstitutional Style Guide (CC BY 4.0), sv.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), the UN Member States page (personal non-commercial use only) and the pages of the central banks of Liberia, Zimbabwe and Timor-Leste and Justia's copy of El Salvador's Ley de Integración Monetaria (all rights reserved or no licence stated) were used only to verify facts that Wikidata gave and to confirm that the author's Swedish forms are in established use: no list, selection or running text was copied from them, and the selection of states follows Wikidata, not their lists. The evidence in the provenance report quotes each source briefly, one state's entry at a time, as citations for verification. Facts such as which currency a state uses, its code and its name are not protected by copyright, so verifying them against these sources puts no conditions on the deck; the EU guide and sv.wikipedia are nonetheless acknowledged as sources.

## Method

1. The research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against Wikidata and against the downloaded reference lists, and with three independent AI reviewers (factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation) whose findings were resolved in quality-control rounds 1–3. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Selection: the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint was asked for every item that is a member (P463) of the United Nations (Q1065) with no end time on that statement (query 1). It returned 203 items; ten are historical predecessor states still tagged as members (Islamic State of Afghanistan, Republic of Afghanistan, Kingdom of Laos, Kingdom of Nepal, Mongolian People's Republic, People's Republic of Mozambique, Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville), Somali Democratic Republic, Third Hellenic Republic, realm of the United Kingdom) and were dropped. The rule: an item without an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (P297) is not a current state. None of the ten has one, while of the other 193 member items only the Kingdom of Denmark (Q756617) lacks one, and it is represented by Denmark (Q35, DK) as described next (query 4); eight of the ten also have a dissolved date (P576), the Third Hellenic Republic and the realm of the United Kingdom have none. Wikidata records the Kingdom of Denmark (Q756617) and the Kingdom of the Netherlands (Q29999) as the members; the cards use Denmark (Q35) and the Netherlands (Q55), the countries whose currency is asked for. The resulting 193 states were compared with the 193 names on the UN's Member States page; they match one to one.
3. Currencies: for the 193 items, Wikidata was asked for every currency (P38) statement that is not deprecated and has no end time, with each currency's ISO 4217 code (P498) and its English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases (query 3); the states' own labels and aliases and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (P297) came from query 2.
4. Cross-checks: the ISO 4217 List One (XML, published 2026-09-17) was downloaded from SIX, the ISO 4217 maintenance agency, and fund codes (IsFund) were set aside. The English and Swedish versions of Annex A5 of the EU Interinstitutional Style Guide (list of countries, territories and currencies) were downloaded and parsed with a short Python script: in each table row of nine or more cells the third cell is the ISO 3166 code, the seventh the currency name and the eighth its ISO 4217 code, and a following three-cell row (name, code, subunit) adds a second currency to the same country; the rows were matched to the states by that ISO 3166 code (EL for Greece and UK for the United Kingdom in EU usage; the Netherlands, whose Wikidata item Q55 has no P297, by hand as NL). SIX entities were matched by name, seven by hand (both Congos are told apart by the code, plus Iran, Moldova, the two Koreas, Micronesia and Venezuela, which ISO writes in its long forms). A card's currency had to be in all three: the Wikidata P38 values, the SIX List One entry for the state and the EU Annex A5 row. For 173 states all three give exactly one currency, with the same code. For 13 more (Chile, Cyprus, France, Ghana, Ireland, Kiribati, Liberia, Lithuania, the Marshall Islands, the Netherlands, Timor-Leste, Tuvalu, Zimbabwe) ISO 4217 and the EU guide give exactly one and Wikidata's P38 includes it among further values (see quality control). For the remaining seven ISO 4217 lists two codes (next paragraph).
5. Countries with more than one currency: where ISO 4217 lists two currencies for a state (Bhutan, El Salvador, Haiti, Lesotho, Namibia, Panama), the card gives the state's own currency and its backNote names the other. The one exception is El Salvador, whose colón the EU style guide describes as "almost no longer used" but still official; that card gives the US dollar, legal tender since the Ley de Integración Monetaria entered into force on 1 January 2001 (Wikidata P580 qualifier, confirmed by the law's Arts. 3 and 25). Venezuela has two ISO codes for the same bolívar soberano (VES and VED); the card gives VES, the code the EU style guide and Wikidata use, and its backNote names VED. For the Netherlands the card gives the euro and the backNote names the currencies of the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom; for France it gives the euro and notes the CFP franc of the French Pacific territories. Where Wikidata lists further currencies that neither ISO 4217 nor the EU style guide lists for the state (see quality control), the card follows ISO 4217 and the EU style guide. Where ISO 4217 lists a single currency but another is also legal tender or in use, the card gives the ISO 4217 currency and a back note names the other, confirmed by the central bank: the US dollar in Liberia (Central Bank of Liberia) and in Zimbabwe's multi-currency system (Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe), and Timor-Leste's own centavo coins beside the US dollar (Banco Central de Timor-Leste). The South African rand in Eswatini, and the Kiribati and Tuvalu coins beside the Australian dollar, are not noted (see quality control round 1).
6. Recent changes the brief asked to watch were checked against SIX: Bulgaria's euro from 1 January 2026 (Amendment 180; BGN in List Three with withdrawal 2026-01), Croatia's euro (HRK withdrawn 2023-01), Sierra Leone's new leone SLE (old SLL withdrawn 2023-12), Zimbabwe Gold ZWG (ZWL withdrawn 2024-09) and Venezuela's VES. Each is current in List One, the EU style guide and Wikidata, and the back notes for Bulgaria, Croatia, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe say what was replaced.
7. English wording: the front is the state's Wikidata English label, except China (the label is the long form "People's Republic of China"). These labels are the common English short names, so some differ from the forms the UN uses (Czech Republic for Czechia, Ivory Coast for Côte d'Ivoire, Cape Verde for Cabo Verde, Turkey for Türkiye); the deck keeps the common names, which every English reader recognises. The back is the currency's English name followed by its ISO code in parentheses, e.g. "Swedish krona (SEK)". The name is the Wikidata English label or one of its English aliases, preferring the form with the nationality adjective (e.g. alias "Afghan afghani" over label "afghani"); nine names are the author's own wording because the label is outdated or malformed and no alias fits: Argentine peso (label "Argentine convertible peso"), Guatemalan quetzal, Haitian gourde, South Korean won, Peruvian sol (label "Nuevo sol"), Venezuelan bolívar (label "sovereign bolivar"), Vanuatu vatu (label "Vanuatu vatus"), Yemeni rial and Zambian kwacha (labels capitalise the unit). Zimbabwe's currency is given by its official name, Zimbabwe Gold (a fact; Wikidata's label is "Zimbabwe ZiG" and its alias "Zimbabwean gold"), which SIX List One and the EU guide confirm.
8. Swedish wording: the front is the state's Wikidata Swedish label, except Eswatini, whose label is still "Swaziland" (the Wikidata alias "Eswatini" is used). The currency name is the Wikidata Swedish label written in lower case, as Swedish writes currency names; 114 names match a Wikidata Swedish label or alias except for the initial capital. The Swedish labels are not uniform (bare units such as forint and rand, adjective + unit such as nigeriansk naira, compounds such as fijidollar), and the deck keeps them as Wikidata gives them, since each is an established Swedish form (the compounds are also the sv.wikipedia article titles) and no single Swedish convention covers all currencies. Where the label is missing or non-standard the author wrote the Swedish name, using the standard pattern of a lower-case nationality adjective and the unit's name, and then checked each form against the EU guide's Swedish list to make sure it is in established use: georgisk lari (label "Georgiska lari"), ghanansk cedi (label "Ghana Cedi"), guineansk franc and komorisk franc (labels "Guinesisk", "Komoransk"), maldivisk rufiyaa (label "Rufiyah"), nepalesisk rupie and pakistansk rupie (labels use the English spelling "rupee"; rupie as in the Wikidata alias "Indisk rupie"), centralafrikansk CFA-franc and västafrikansk CFA-franc (labels "Centralafrikansk CFA Franc" and "CFA Franc"; the West African franc needs its qualifier to be told apart), venezuelansk bolívar (no Swedish label) and zimbabwiskt guld (no Swedish label; the author's literal translation of the official name Zimbabwe Gold, zimbabwisk + guld in the neuter). All but västafrikansk CFA-franc occur in the EU guide's Swedish list (as "venezuelansk bolívar soberano" for the bolívar); these are short names of facts, and no list was taken from the guide. Two Swedish names were changed in review round 2: tongansk paʻanga (the Wikidata label writes an ASCII apostrophe; the ʻokina is used as in the English label and on sv.wikipedia), and dobra (the bare unit, as on sv.wikipedia, instead of the label "Saotomeansk Dobra"). The US dollar is "amerikansk dollar" (a Wikidata alias; the label is the plural-looking "amerikanska dollar"), the euro is "euro" (Wikidata's multilingual label). The ISO code is the same in both languages.
9. Machine checks: every card carries Wikidata checks that the builder runs against live Wikidata: the state's P38 includes the card's currency item, the currency's P498 is the card's code, and, wherever the card text is a Wikidata label or alias, that the English or Swedish text is one. 1011 checks in all, 624 of them on labels. Every card also has evidence entries quoting what Wikidata, SIX List One and the EU Annex A5 row say for that state, generated from the downloaded files; evidence added in the review rounds was written by hand from the pages cited.
10. Excluded: states that are not UN members (e.g. Kosovo, Taiwan, the Holy See, Palestine), dependent territories, fund codes and units of account (e.g. CLF, BOV, MXV, CHE, CHW, USN, UYI, UYW), cryptocurrencies, and currencies Wikidata lists but ISO 4217 does not list for the state.

## Selection

All 193 member states of the United Nations, one card each, as recorded in Wikidata (member of Q1065 with no end time, and with an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code) and confirmed against the UN's Member States page; Denmark and the Netherlands stand for their Kingdoms. Each card gives the currency the state officially uses today according to ISO 4217 List One as published on 2026-09-17, confirmed by Wikidata and the EU Interinstitutional Style Guide. Where ISO 4217 lists two currencies, the state's own currency is given and the other is named in a back note (El Salvador, whose own colón is almost no longer used, gets the US dollar). Where ISO 4217 lists one currency but another is also legal tender or in use (Liberia, Zimbabwe, Timor-Leste's own coins), the card gives ISO 4217's single listing and a back note names the other. Left out: non-member states and territories, fund codes and units of account, cryptocurrencies, and currencies that Wikidata lists but ISO 4217 does not assign to the state.

## Queries

**Query 1: UN member states with their currencies, codes, ranks and start/end times (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv ?currency ?currencyEn ?currencySv ?code ?rank ?start ?end WHERE {
  ?country p:P463 ?m .
  ?m ps:P463 wd:Q1065 .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?m pq:P582 ?mEnd }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?country p:P38 ?st .
    ?st ps:P38 ?currency ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
    OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
    OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
    OPTIONAL { ?currency wdt:P498 ?code }
    OPTIONAL { ?currency rdfs:label ?currencyEn FILTER(LANG(?currencyEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?currency rdfs:label ?currencySv FILTER(LANG(?currencySv) = "sv") }
  }
}
ORDER BY ?countryEn
```

  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  FILTER(?rank != wikibase:DeprecatedRank)
  OPTIONAL { ?currency wdt:P498 ?code }
  VALUES ?lang { "en" "sv" "mul" }
  { ?currency rdfs:label ?text BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?currency skos:altLabel ?text BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) = ?lang)
}
```

**How queries 1–3 were run (query file in the scratch directory)** (Wikidata)

```

FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?m pq:P582 ?e } OPTIONAL { ?c wdt:P576 ?dis } OPTIONAL { ?c wdt:P1366 ?rb } OPTIONAL { ?c wdt:P297 ?p297 } OPTIONAL { ?c rdfs:label ?cEn FILTER(LANG(?cEn)="en") } } GROUP BY ?c ?cEn' https://query.wikidata.org/sparql

## Quality control

5 rounds, 40 findings: 27 fixed, 3 rejected after checking, 10 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (1011 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Machine and source checks: every card's currency and code compared across Wikidata, ISO 4217 List One (SIX) and the EU style guide's Annex A5; Wikidata checks run by the builder. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 193 cards.

For 185 of the 193 states Wikidata, SIX and the EU guide agree on a single currency and code. The other eight (Bhutan, El Salvador, Haiti, Lesotho, Namibia, Panama, Venezuela, the Netherlands) have a second currency or code in one of the sources and are handled by the stated rule with a back note. The builder's 1004 Wikidata checks (618 on labels) pass. Discrepancies where Wikidata disagrees with ISO 4217 and the EU guide are listed below; in each the card follows ISO 4217 and the EU guide, and no Wikidata check was written for the disputed value. [Correction from QC round 1: the first sentence overstated the agreement. For 173 states all three sources give exactly one and the same code; for 13 more ISO 4217 and the EU guide give one code and Wikidata's P38 includes it among further values; ISO 4217 lists two codes for the other seven. The Method states the corrected figures.]

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|

ISO 4217 List One and the EU guide list only Zimbabwe Gold (ZWG). | The card gives Zimbabwe Gold (ZWG), whose P38 statement exists in Wikidata; the back note says it replaced the Zimbabwe dollar (ZWL), withdrawn from ISO 4217 in 2024-09. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 193 cards: every card's ISO 4217 code against a fresh download of List One, the back notes on recent changes against List Three and Amendment 180, and the builder's live Wikidata checks.

The reviewer found no wrong answers: every code is the current ISO 4217 code for its state, the back notes on Bulgaria, Croatia, Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe and Venezuela are accurate, and all Wikidata checks pass. It found two multi-currency states without a back note (Zimbabwe, Liberia), an overstated agreement count in the round-0 summary and the Method, an inaccurate France note, and suggested optional notes for Eswatini, Timor-Leste, Kiribati and Tuvalu. Zimbabwe, Liberia, the count, France and Timor-Leste were fixed; the others were declined.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| zimbabwe | The card gives only Zimbabwe Gold (ZWG); its back note does not say that Zimbabwe runs a multi-currency system in which the US dollar is also used, and the selection states no rule for such cases. | Verified: the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's Mid-Term Monetary Policy Statement of 7 August 2025 (para. 200, p. 94; feedback table p. 106) speaks of "the multicurrency system" and of "transacting in USD" (text extracted from the PDF; the 2026 statements are image-only scans and could not be searched). The back note now reads (en) "Introduced in 2024 as ZiG, replacing the Zimbabwe dollar (ZWL), which ISO 4217 withdrew in September 2024. Zimbabwe has a multi-currency system in which the US dollar is also used.", with matching Swedish; the RBZ statement is added as a verification source. The note does not call the US dollar legal tender, because no RBZ text seen says so in those words. The selection and Method now state the rule: ISO 4217's single listing on the card, other legal tender or currency in use in a back note. | fixed |
| liberia | The card has no back note although the US dollar is legal tender in Liberia beside the Liberian dollar. | Verified: the Central Bank of Liberia's 2007 financial statements (p. 23) say the U.S. dollar "has been legal tender in the country since then", and the CBL's 2017 perspective on the House bill to amend section 19 of the CBL Act calls the arrangement "the dual currency regime". That bill (US dollar legal tender only for foreign obligations) passed the House in 2017; no evidence was found that it became law, and a FrontPage Africa report of 3 July 2019 (https://frontpageafricaonline.com/commerce-ministry-mandates-all-business-transactions-be-done-in-liberian-and-united-states-dollars/) quotes the Commerce Minister: "It (USD) is a legal tender". The reviewer's quote of section 19.2 from a search summary turned out to be the bill's proposed wording, so the CBL Act itself is not cited. Back note added: "The US dollar is also legal tender in Liberia (a dual-currency system); the card gives Liberia's own currency." (with Swedish), with the CBL as a verification source. Wikidata lists the US dollar (Q4917) as a normal-rank P38 value beside the preferred Liberian dollar (quoted in the card's Wikidata evidence); the builder's property check reads only best-rank values, so no check was written for it. The round-0 Liberia finding ('no change needed') is superseded by this one. | fixed |
| deck | The round-0 summary and the Method say that for 185 states Wikidata, SIX and the EU guide agree on a single currency and code, but the round's own findings list further Wikidata P38 values for several of those states. | Recounted from the combined data: for 173 states all three sources give exactly one currency with the same code; for 13 (Chile, Cyprus, France, Ghana, Ireland, Kiribati, Liberia, Lithuania, the Marshall Islands, the Netherlands, Timor-Leste, Tuvalu, Zimbabwe) ISO 4217 and the EU guide give one and Wikidata's P38 includes it among further values; ISO 4217 lists two codes for the remaining seven. The recount found three states not in the round-0 findings: Wikidata also lists the "Irish euro coin" (Q274474) for Ireland, the Lithuanian talonas (Q1130620, LTT, a 1990s transitional currency without an end time) for Lithuania and the "Ghana Pesewa" subunit (Q134397947) for Ghana; none is a current ISO 4217 currency, and the cards (euro, euro, Ghana cedi) stand. The Method now gives the corrected figures, and a correction is appended to the round-0 summary. | fixed |
| france | The back note calls France's Pacific CFP-franc territories "overseas collectivities", but New Caledonia is a sui generis collectivity, not an overseas collectivity. | Accepted. The note now names the three territories without a status: "France's Pacific territories (French Polynesia, New Caledonia, Wallis and Futuna) use the CFP franc (XPF)." / "Frankrikes territorier i Stilla havet (Franska Polynesien, Nya Kaledonien, Wallis- och Futunaöarna) använder CFP-franc (XPF)." The territory names are the Wikidata en and sv labels, with six label checks added; SIX List One lists XPF for all three. | fixed |
| eswatini | Lesotho and Namibia get a note on the South African rand, but Eswatini, the third Common Monetary Area member, gets none. | Declined. ISO 4217 and the EU guide list only SZL for Eswatini, so the card differs from Lesotho and Namibia for a stated reason (ISO lists the rand for those two). Whether the rand is legal tender in Eswatini varies between sources, as the reviewer notes, and no current Central Bank of Eswatini statement could be retrieved to support a note on the peg or circulation; the quality bar asks to leave out contested facts. | rejected |
| timor-leste | Timor-Leste's central bank issues its own centavo coins beside the US dollar; Kiribati and Tuvalu have their own coins beside the Australian dollar. The cards carry no note (optional). | Timor-Leste: added the note "Timor-Leste also issues its own centavo coins, equal in value to US cents." (with Swedish), confirmed by the Banco Central de Timor-Leste's coins page (issued since 10 November 2003, 100 centavos = 100 US cents) and Wikidata's P38 value "East Timor centavo coins" (Q572213, now a check). Kiribati and Tuvalu: declined, since no current issuing authority's statement on those coins circulating today was found and Wikidata's items (Kiribati dollar, Tuvaluan dollar) carry no ISO code; the cards give the Australian dollar as ISO 4217 does. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language and translation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language and translation reviewer · **Scope:** All 193 cards, front and back in English and Swedish, the back notes, title, description, keywords and the language tags in the built deck.

The reviewer found the language in good shape: all text is tagged correctly, Swedish currency names are lower case and the Swedish country names are the established forms. It raised one warning (an ASCII apostrophe in the Swedish Tonga name) and seven suggestions. Tonga, São Tomé and Príncipe, the Bulgaria and Croatia notes and the El Salvador note were changed, and the conventions for English fronts and Swedish currency names are now stated in the Method; the Paraguay accent, the Turkmenistan name and the alignment of the Swedish dollar compounds were declined.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| tonga | The Swedish back writes "tongansk pa'anga" with an ASCII apostrophe while the English side uses the ʻokina. | Verified on sv.wikipedia (article Paʻanga), which writes paʻanga and says the name is written with the ʻokina "och alltså inte en vanlig apostrof". back.sv is now "tongansk paʻanga (TOP)"; sv.wikipedia is added as a verification source. The card had no Swedish label check, so none was dropped; the Method records the departure from the Wikidata label. | fixed |
| paraguay | The Swedish back "guarani (PYG)" drops the accent that the EU guide and the English side keep. | Declined: the unaccented form is the established Swedish spelling. The Wikidata Swedish label is "Guarani", and sv.wikipedia's article is titled "Guarani (valuta)" ("Paraguayansk guarani" redirects to it) and writes "Guarani … är den valuta som används i Paraguay"; this evidence is added to the card. With the code on the card the name cannot be confused with the people or language. | rejected |
| sao-tome-and-principe | "saotomeansk dobra" comes only from the Wikidata Swedish label and is a rare form; the EU guide and sv.wikipedia say "dobra". | Accepted: back.sv is now "dobra (STN)", the bare unit, as in sv.wikipedia's article "Dobra (valuta)" (evidence added) and the EU guide's Swedish list; the card had no Swedish label check to replace. | fixed |
| bulgaria | The Swedish notes for Bulgaria and Croatia are subjectless fragments copying the English participle ("Sedan den 1 januari 2026; ersatte bulgarisk lev (BGN)."); the same applies to croatia. | Accepted for both cards: "Sedan den 1 januari 2026, då euron ersatte bulgarisk lev (BGN)." and "Sedan den 1 januari 2023, då euron ersatte kroatisk kuna (HRK)." The Zimbabwe note, which had the same construction, was rewritten as a full sentence in round 1 ("Infördes 2024 som ZiG och ersatte …"). | fixed |
| el-salvador | "används nästan inte längre" is a literal rendering; idiomatic Swedish is "används knappt längre". | Accepted: the note now ends "… men används knappt längre." | fixed |
| turkmenistan | "Turkmenistan new manat (TMT)" keeps "new", unlike Azerbaijani manat or Sierra Leonean leone. | Declined: "Turkmenistan New Manat" is the currency's name in ISO 4217 List One and the Wikidata English label, just as "Israeli new shekel" is kept; Azerbaijan's ISO 4217 name is "Azerbaijan Manat", without "new", so the deck follows the official names consistently. The card keeps its English label check. | rejected |
| deck | The English fronts mix current official short names (Eswatini, North Macedonia, Timor-Leste) with common exonyms the UN no longer uses (Czech Republic, Ivory Coast, Cape Verde, Turkey), with no stated rule. | The convention is now stated in the Method's English-wording step: the fronts are the Wikidata English labels, the common English short names, which for these four differ from the UN forms (Czechia, Côte d'Ivoire, Cabo Verde, Türkiye). The fronts are unchanged; no front notes were added, since each name is unambiguous. | fixed |
| deck | The Swedish currency names mix bare units, adjective + unit and compounds (fijidollar, salomondollar, trinidaddollar), and the Method claims some names were "chosen for consistency". | The Method no longer claims consistency; it now says the Swedish names are the Wikidata Swedish labels in lower case, which vary because Swedish usage varies, and that each is an established form (the compounds are also sv.wikipedia article titles, e.g. Trinidaddollar). Aligning the compounds with the EU guide's "fijiansk dollar" pattern was declined: it would replace a Wikidata form by one taken from a verification source without making the card more correct. | fixed |

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** All 193 cards' wording against Wikidata and the EU Swedish table; every source's licence page; the recorded queries against the query files; SIX and EU downloads re-fetched and compared; the Method's reproducibility.

The reviewer found the provenance record honest and checkable (licence quotes verbatim, downloads byte-identical, queries as run), but the dossier said that the Zimbabwe names and ten Swedish names came from verification-only sources, contradicting the CC0 licensing paragraph; it also asked to record the EU guide's licence as CC BY 4.0, and suggested notes on the SIX quotations, the SIX URL and downloads, and reproducibility. All were addressed by rewording the Method and licensing to say what was done, correcting the source records and adding the missing rules and commands; the deck stays CC0.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| zimbabwe | The Method says "Zimbabwe Gold" and "zimbabwiskt guld" follow SIX and the EU guide, which are verification-only sources, while the licensing paragraph says no text was copied; neither name is a Wikidata label. | Fixed by stating what the names are. "Zimbabwe Gold" is the currency's official name, a fact; Wikidata (the content source) gives the currency item, its code and the alias "Zimbabwean gold", and SIX and the EU guide confirm the official name. "zimbabwiskt guld" is the author's literal Swedish translation of that name (zimbabwisk + guld, neuter), which the EU guide's Swedish list also uses; the Method now says so rather than calling it "the EU guide's Swedish name". No RBZ document with the name in a text layer was found, so none is cited for it. Relicensing the deck under CC BY 4.0 was not needed, since a currency's name is not protected expression. | fixed |
